name: Huddle Core
description: Built-in DFIR plays organized by the PICERL incident response lifecycle.

plays.title: Confirm IR roles and call tree
plays.summary: Make sure everyone knows who leads, who decides, and how to reach them, including after hours.
steps: Identify the incident commander and a deputy
Confirm technical leads for endpoint, identity, network and cloud
Verify the executive, legal, HR and communications contacts
Test the call tree and update stale numbers

plays.title: Establish out-of-band communications
plays.summary: Assume corporate email and chat may be watched by the attacker. Stand up a separate channel.
steps: Pick a channel outside the corporate identity provider (e.g. Signal group or separate tenant)
Share a bridge line or meeting link that does not rely on compromised accounts
Agree a codename for the incident
Tell responders not to discuss the incident on corporate channels

plays.title: Verify logging coverage and retention
plays.summary: Confirm the telemetry you will need exists and is retained long enough to investigate.
steps: Check EDR deployment coverage against the asset inventory
Confirm Windows Security, PowerShell and Sysmon logs forward to the SIEM
Confirm identity provider, email and cloud audit logs are enabled
Extend retention on relevant sources before they roll over

plays.title: Validate offline and immutable backups
plays.summary: Know that clean, restorable backups exist before you need them.
steps: Confirm at least one copy is offline or immutable
Check backup console credentials are not domain-joined or shared
Test-restore a representative system
Record backup schedules and the latest known-good restore points

plays.title: Stage forensic jump kit
plays.summary: Have collection tools, storage and write blockers ready before an incident.
steps: Stage triage collectors (KAPE, Velociraptor) and memory capture tools
Prepare encrypted, wiped external storage
Confirm hardware write blockers work
Keep chain-of-custody forms and hashing utilities with the kit

plays.title: Maintain crown-jewel asset inventory
plays.summary: Know which systems and data matter most so you can prioritize scoping and recovery.
steps: List critical business systems and their owners
Map where sensitive and regulated data lives
Document dependencies (identity, DNS, backups)
Agree recovery priority order with the business

plays.title: Activate IR retainer
plays.summary: Engage an outside incident response firm early when the incident exceeds internal capacity.
steps: Contact the retainer firm through the agreed process
Route the engagement through counsel where privilege matters
Share scope, timeline and access requirements
Agree reporting cadence and deliverables

plays.title: Triage the initial alert
plays.summary: Decide whether the alert is a true positive and how serious it looks.
steps: Review the alert details, the affected host and user
Pull surrounding telemetry for 24 hours either side
Check whether indicators match known threat intelligence
Record your finding: false positive, benign true positive, or incident

plays.title: Declare incident and assign severity
plays.summary: Formally declare the incident so the right people, budget and authority come into play.
steps: Apply your severity matrix (impact × scope × data sensitivity)
Name the incident commander
Kick off the out-of-band bridge
Set the first update time for leadership

plays.title: Open case record and evidence log
plays.summary: Start the running record of decisions, actions and evidence from the first minute.
steps: Create the case ticket with a unique incident ID
Start a timestamped action log (UTC)
Start a chain-of-custody log for every evidence item
Store hashes for all collected evidence

plays.title: Engage legal counsel
plays.summary: Bring in counsel early to protect privilege and guide notification decisions.
steps: Notify in-house or outside counsel
Decide whether the investigation runs under privilege
Agree how findings are written and shared
Flag any contractual notification clauses

plays.title: Notify cyber insurance carrier
plays.summary: Many policies require prompt notice and approval of vendors before costs are covered.
steps: Locate the policy and the claims hotline
Report the incident within the policy notice window
Confirm which IR, legal and negotiation vendors are pre-approved
Track all incident costs from the start

plays.title: Assess notification obligations
plays.summary: Work out which regulators, customers and partners may need to be told, and by when.
steps: Identify the data types and jurisdictions involved
List regulatory clocks (e.g. GDPR 72 hours after awareness; SEC 8-K Item 1.05 within four business days of a materiality determination)
Review customer and partner contract obligations
Document the decision and its reasoning with counsel

plays.title: Capture volatile memory
plays.summary: Collect RAM before rebooting or isolating so in-memory malware, keys and connections are preserved.
steps: Run a memory capture tool from external media
Hash the image and log it in chain of custody
Collect running processes and network connections as a quick fallback
Analyze with Volatility for injected code, network artifacts and credentials

plays.title: Run triage collection
plays.summary: Pull high-value artifacts quickly from affected endpoints without a full image.
steps: Run a triage target set across the affected hosts
Include event logs, registry hives, $MFT, $UsnJrnl, Prefetch, Amcache, SRUM, browser and LNK files
Hash and store collections centrally
Parse with standard tooling for timeline analysis

plays.title: Acquire full disk image
plays.summary: Create a forensically sound copy when deep analysis or legal action is likely.
steps: Decide physical vs. logical image based on encryption and urgency
Use a write blocker for physical media; snapshot for VMs and cloud disks
Verify image hashes match the source
Record acquisition in chain of custody

plays.title: Hunt for lateral movement
plays.summary: Find where the attacker moved and which credentials they used to get there.
steps: Review logons 4624 (types 3 and 10), 4648, 4672 and 4776
Look for new services (7045) and scheduled tasks (4698)
Check RDP, SMB, WinRM, WMI and PsExec activity between hosts
Map source → destination host pairs into a graph

plays.title: Build incident timeline
plays.summary: Merge evidence into one timeline so the story of the intrusion is clear.
steps: Generate a super timeline from triage and disk artifacts
Pivot on known-bad times, users, files and hosts
Mark key events: initial access, execution, persistence, movement, impact
Keep the timeline in UTC and cite the source of every row

plays.title: Review persistence mechanisms
plays.summary: Find every way the attacker could come back after a reboot or password reset.
steps: Check Run/RunOnce keys, services, scheduled tasks and startup folders
Check WMI event subscriptions and COM hijacks
Review new or modified local and domain accounts
Compare autoruns against a known-good baseline

plays.title: Review identity provider sign-ins
plays.summary: Look for account takeover in cloud identity logs.
steps: Pull sign-in logs for the affected users (Entra ID / Okta / Google)
Look for impossible travel, new devices, anonymizing IPs and legacy protocols
Check for MFA fatigue patterns and newly registered MFA methods
Identify every IP and session tied to the attacker

plays.title: Investigate mailbox activity
plays.summary: Work out what an attacker did inside a compromised mailbox.
steps: Search the unified audit log for the affected mailbox
List inbox rules, forwarding settings and delegates
Review MailItemsAccessed / Send events to see what was read and sent
Check for OAuth applications granted by the user

plays.title: Analyze suspicious file
plays.summary: Understand what a malicious file does and pull out indicators.
steps: Hash the sample and check reputation services
Run static triage: strings, imports, signatures, packing
Detonate in an isolated sandbox
Extract IOCs: domains, IPs, mutexes, dropped files, registry changes

plays.title: Review network telemetry
plays.summary: Use network logs to find command-and-control traffic and data leaving the environment.
steps: Search firewall, proxy and DNS logs for known indicators
Look for beaconing (regular intervals, consistent sizes)
Look for large outbound transfers and unusual destinations
Identify every internal host talking to attacker infrastructure

plays.title: Determine data exfiltration scope
plays.summary: Figure out what data may have been taken, which drives notification and extortion response.
steps: Look for staging (archives, rclone, MEGA, cloud storage tools)
Correlate outbound volumes with the timeline
Identify file shares and databases the attacker accessed
Document what was confirmed vs. what is possible

plays.title: Identify initial access vector
plays.summary: Find how the attacker got in so the door can be closed.
steps: Work backwards on the timeline to the earliest malicious event
Check phishing, exposed services, VPN and stolen credentials
Review vulnerability scans for exploitable internet-facing systems
Confirm the vector with at least two independent evidence sources

plays.title: Review cloud control-plane logs
plays.summary: Look for attacker actions against your cloud accounts and resources.
steps: Pull CloudTrail, Azure Activity / Entra audit, or GCP audit logs
Look for new IAM users, keys, roles and policy changes
Look for unusual regions, instance launches and storage access
Identify all access keys and principals the attacker used

plays.title: Hunt for credential dumping
plays.summary: Check whether the attacker harvested passwords or hashes, which widens the reset scope.
steps: Look for LSASS access and dumps (procdump, comsvcs.dll MiniDump)
Look for NTDS.dit extraction or DCSync (4662 with replication GUIDs)
Check for Kerberoasting (4769 with RC4)
List every account whose credentials may be exposed

plays.title: Extract and share IOCs
plays.summary: Package indicators so blocking, hunting and partners can use them.
steps: Collect hashes, domains, IPs, file paths, user agents and account names
Remove false positives and internal infrastructure
Load indicators into the TIP/MISP with context and confidence
Push to blocking and hunting teams

plays.title: Identify ransomware variant
plays.summary: Knowing the family tells you its usual behavior, leak site and whether a decryptor exists.
steps: Collect the ransom note and an encrypted sample file
Identify the family (ID Ransomware, vendor reports)
Check No More Ransom for a free decryptor
Check the group's leak site for victim posting

plays.title: Review web server logs and hunt web shells
plays.summary: Find exploitation of a public-facing application and any web shells left behind.
steps: Search access logs for exploit patterns and unusual POSTs to static paths
List recently created or modified files in web roots
Look for web server processes spawning shells
Compare deployed code to source control

plays.title: Review user activity for insider risk
plays.summary: Investigate possible malicious or negligent insider activity carefully and with HR and legal.
steps: Confirm authorization with HR and legal before searching
Review DLP, file access and USB/cloud upload activity
Correlate with access badges and HR events (resignation, PIP)
Keep the investigation need-to-know

plays.title: Preserve evidence before containment
plays.summary: Some containment steps destroy evidence. Capture it first when time allows.
steps: Snapshot affected VMs and cloud disks
Capture memory on key hosts
Export logs that may roll over
Record exactly what will be changed and when

plays.title: Isolate host with EDR
plays.summary: Cut a compromised endpoint off from the network while keeping EDR access for investigation.
steps: Confirm the host and its business owner
Trigger EDR network containment
Verify isolation (no outbound except the EDR cloud)
Record the isolation time in the case log

plays.title: Disable compromised accounts
plays.summary: Stop the attacker from using known-compromised user and service accounts.
steps: Disable the accounts in AD and the cloud identity provider
Coordinate with service owners before disabling service accounts
Notify the affected users through a verified channel
Record every account action

plays.title: Reset credentials and revoke sessions
plays.summary: A password reset alone leaves stolen tokens working. Revoke sessions too.
steps: Reset passwords for the affected accounts
Revoke refresh tokens and active sessions (e.g. Revoke-MgUserSignInSession, Okta clear sessions)
Remove attacker-registered MFA methods and devices
Monitor for re-authentication from attacker IPs

plays.title: Block IOCs at controls
plays.summary: Push confirmed indicators to every control that can block them.
steps: Block domains and IPs at the firewall, proxy and DNS
Add file hashes to EDR block lists
Block sender domains and URLs at the email gateway
Set alerts for any further hits

plays.title: Remove malicious mail rules and purge phishing
plays.summary: Clean the attacker's mailbox changes and pull the phishing email from every inbox.
steps: Delete malicious inbox rules, forwarding and delegates
Search all mailboxes for the phishing message
Purge matching messages tenant-wide
Identify users who clicked or replied

plays.title: Revoke malicious OAuth consent
plays.summary: Remove third-party apps the attacker used to keep access without a password.
steps: List enterprise applications and user consents for the affected users
Revoke grants for suspicious apps
Disable the service principal tenant-wide
Restrict user consent to verified publishers

plays.title: Restrict lateral movement paths
plays.summary: Limit the attacker's ability to spread between systems.
steps: Block SMB, RDP and WinRM between workstations
Restrict admin access to jump hosts only
Segment critical servers with temporary firewall rules
Monitor denied connections for attacker activity

plays.title: Rotate privileged and service account credentials
plays.summary: Assume privileged credentials are exposed once the attacker has admin rights.
steps: Rotate domain admin, enterprise admin and tier-0 credentials
Rotate service account passwords with owners
Rotate local admin passwords (LAPS)
Rotate secrets in vaults and CI/CD

plays.title: Reset KRBTGT twice
plays.summary: Invalidate forged Kerberos tickets (golden tickets) after domain compromise.
steps: Confirm AD replication is healthy
Reset the KRBTGT password once
Wait until the reset has replicated to every DC and at least the maximum ticket lifetime has passed (10 hours by default)
Reset it a second time and monitor for authentication errors

plays.title: Protect backups from the attacker
plays.summary: Attackers target backups to force payment. Lock them down immediately.
steps: Disconnect or lock the backup infrastructure
Rotate backup console credentials
Enable immutability where possible
Verify the latest clean restore points still exist

plays.title: Cut internet egress
plays.summary: A last-resort step to stop exfiltration or encryption spreading through C2.
steps: Get executive approval with business impact noted
Block outbound at the perimeter except approved IR tooling
Keep EDR and logging channels open
Plan staged restoration of egress

plays.title: Disable unauthorized remote access paths
plays.summary: Close the remote access the attacker used or could use.
steps: Block attacker IPs on VPN and disable affected VPN accounts
Remove internet exposure of RDP and other admin services
Block unapproved RMM tools (AnyDesk, ScreenConnect, etc.)
Require MFA on all remaining remote access

plays.title: Rotate cloud access keys and secrets
plays.summary: Deactivate keys the attacker used and rotate anything they could have read.
steps: Deactivate compromised access keys and service principal secrets
Rotate secrets in parameter stores and key vaults
Remove attacker-created IAM users, roles and policies
Apply SCPs or conditional access to block attacker regions or IPs

plays.title: Take vulnerable application offline or virtual-patch
plays.summary: Stop ongoing exploitation of a public-facing application.
steps: Apply a WAF rule or take the service offline
Put up a maintenance page and notify stakeholders
Preserve logs and a disk snapshot first
Track the exposure window for scoping

plays.title: Remove malware and persistence
plays.summary: Remove every malicious file and persistence mechanism found during analysis.
steps: Delete malicious binaries, scripts and web shells
Remove malicious services, tasks, run keys and WMI subscriptions
Remove attacker-created accounts
Document every removal with path and hash

plays.title: Reimage compromised hosts
plays.summary: When in doubt, rebuild. Reimaging is more reliable than cleaning.
steps: Confirm evidence collection is complete
Wipe and reimage from a known-good gold image
Patch fully before reconnecting
Restore user data from clean sources only

plays.title: Patch the exploited vulnerability
plays.summary: Close the vulnerability that allowed initial access or escalation.
steps: Confirm the CVE and affected versions
Apply the vendor patch or mitigation
Scan to confirm the fix
Check for other systems with the same exposure

plays.title: Remove unauthorized access
plays.summary: Clean up any access the attacker granted themselves.
steps: Audit privileged groups for unexpected members
Remove rogue accounts, keys, certificates and app registrations
Review GPO and conditional access changes during the intrusion window
Review delegated and federated trust changes

plays.title: Remove unauthorized remote access tools
plays.summary: Uninstall the RMM and tunneling tools attackers commonly leave behind.
steps: Inventory remote access software across the fleet
Uninstall anything not on the approved list
Remove tunnels (ngrok, Cloudflared, Chisel) and proxies
Add application control rules to prevent reinstall

plays.title: Validate eradication with a fleet sweep
plays.summary: Prove the attacker is gone before you start recovery.
steps: Re-sweep all hosts for every known IOC and TTP
Run YARA and hunting queries across the fleet
Confirm no new C2 traffic for an agreed quiet period
Get IR lead sign-off to move to recovery

plays.title: Harden exploited configurations
plays.summary: Fix the weak settings the attacker relied on.
steps: Disable legacy authentication protocols
Remove excessive admin rights and local admin from users
Enable credential protections (LSA protection, Credential Guard)
Apply attack surface reduction rules

plays.title: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA
plays.summary: Upgrade MFA for affected and privileged users so stolen passwords and push fatigue stop working.
steps: Require MFA for all affected users
Move privileged users to FIDO2 or certificate-based MFA
Turn on number matching for push MFA where it is not already enforced
Block MFA registration from untrusted locations

plays.title: Restore from clean backups
plays.summary: Bring systems back from backups taken before the compromise.
steps: Pick restore points that predate the earliest attacker activity
Restore to an isolated network first
Scan restored systems for IOCs before reconnecting
Restore in the agreed business priority order

plays.title: Recover Active Directory
plays.summary: When AD itself is untrustworthy, recover it in a controlled way.
steps: Choose between targeted cleanup and full forest recovery
Restore a DC from a clean backup in isolation
Seize roles, clean metadata and reset tier-0 credentials
Rebuild other DCs from the recovered one

plays.title: Use vendor decryptor
plays.summary: If a reliable decryptor exists, test it carefully before wide use.
steps: Get the decryptor from a trusted source (No More Ransom, vendor)
Test on copies of encrypted files first
Check decrypted files for integrity
Rebuild the host anyway once data is recovered

plays.title: Staged return to production
plays.summary: Reconnect in stages so a missed foothold is caught quickly.
steps: Reconnect the highest-priority systems first
Watch each stage for an agreed period before the next
Restore internet egress last if it was cut
Keep a rollback plan for each stage

plays.title: Validate business functionality
plays.summary: Have business owners confirm systems work before declaring recovery.
steps: Run owner-defined acceptance checks
Confirm data integrity and the last good transaction
Confirm integrations and dependencies
Get written sign-off from each owner

plays.title: Enhanced monitoring period
plays.summary: Watch closely for re-entry for weeks after recovery.
steps: Add detections for every observed TTP and IOC
Lower alert thresholds on the affected systems and accounts
Schedule daily hunts for the next 30 days
Watch leak sites and credential dumps for your organization

plays.title: Restore user access and communicate
plays.summary: Bring people back to work with clear instructions.
steps: Issue new credentials through a verified process
Tell users what happened at an appropriate level
Give instructions for reporting anything suspicious
Staff the help desk for the expected volume

plays.title: Hold post-incident review
plays.summary: Run a blameless review while memories are fresh, ideally within two weeks.
steps: Invite responders, owners and leadership
Walk the timeline: what happened, what went well, what didn't
Identify root causes and contributing factors
Agree concrete actions with owners and dates

plays.title: Write final incident report
plays.summary: Produce the record of the incident for leadership, auditors and future responders.
steps: Executive summary with impact and root cause
Detailed timeline with evidence references
Actions taken by phase
Recommendations and their status

plays.title: Turn findings into detections
plays.summary: Make sure the same attack would be caught earlier next time.
steps: Write detections for each observed TTP
Test them against the incident evidence
Map coverage to MITRE ATT&CK
Add regression tests to the detection pipeline

plays.title: Track remediation to closure
plays.summary: Recommendations only matter if they get done.
steps: Log each action in the work tracker
Assign owners and due dates
Review progress at a regular cadence
Escalate overdue high-risk items

plays.title: Update playbooks and IR plan
plays.summary: Feed what you learned back into your playbooks, including this one.
steps: Update steps that were missing, wrong or slow
Update contacts and vendor details
Re-export and re-share the updated Huddle playbook
Schedule a tabletop to test the changes

plays.title: Archive evidence per retention policy
plays.summary: Keep evidence as long as legal and regulatory needs require, then dispose of it properly.
steps: Confirm legal hold requirements with counsel
Move evidence to secure, access-controlled storage
Verify hashes after transfer
Record the retention date and disposal method

plays.title: Capture incident metrics
plays.summary: Measure response so you can show improvement over time.
steps: Record time to detect, contain, eradicate and recover
Record dwell time and the systems affected
Record total cost including third parties
Compare against previous incidents

plays.title: Share intelligence with peers
plays.summary: Help others defend against the same actor.
steps: Get legal approval for what can be shared
Sanitize indicators and TTPs
Share with your ISAC or trusted partners
Consider reporting to law enforcement (e.g. FBI IC3)

plays.title: Investigate a software supply chain compromise
plays.summary: A vendor update, package or build pipeline you trust may have shipped malicious code.
steps: Identify the affected product, versions and hashes from the vendor advisory or your own analysis
Find every host that installed an affected version, and when
Hunt for the reported post-install behavior: child processes, outbound domains, new services
Check your own build systems and package mirrors for the same dependency

plays.title: Handle an extortion or leak-site claim
plays.summary: An attacker claims to hold your data, by email or on a leak site, with or without encryption.
steps: Do not reply or negotiate until counsel and leadership decide how to proceed
Preserve the message, headers, leak-site posts and any samples
Verify the samples against your data to judge whether the claim is real
Run sanctions screening with counsel before any payment discussion (in the US, OFAC)
Scope how the data was taken using the exfiltration plays

plays.title: Respond to a lost or stolen device
plays.summary: A laptop or phone with company data is missing. Work out what it held and whether it was protected.
steps: Confirm the device, owner, time and place it went missing
Check MDM for disk encryption status, last check-in and passcode compliance
List the data and cached credentials it could hold
Decide on remote lock or wipe with the owner and counsel

plays.title: Mitigate a DDoS attack
plays.summary: Keep services available under a denial-of-service attack.
steps: Confirm it is an attack, not a traffic spike or failure, with network and app metrics
Engage your DDoS protection provider or ISP and turn on emergency mitigation
Apply rate limits, geo or ASN blocks, and caching at the edge
Watch for a second attack using the DDoS as cover

plays.title: Block an untrusted software update
plays.summary: Stop a compromised update or package from spreading further.
steps: Block the affected hashes and update domains in EDR and the proxy
Pause automatic updates for the product and pin known-good versions
Isolate hosts showing post-install malicious behavior
Follow the vendor's guidance, but verify their indicators yourself

plays.title: Communicate with customers and partners
plays.summary: Tell the people affected what happened, what it means for them and what to do.
steps: Agree the facts, the message and the timing with counsel and communications
Prepare FAQs, a help line or mailbox, and support team scripts
Notify regulators and individuals in the windows your assessment found
Publish updates on a predictable schedule until closure

templates.name: Ransomware
templates.description: Encryption event across endpoints and servers, possible data theft.

templates.name: Business Email Compromise
templates.description: Mailbox takeover used for fraud, invoice redirection or internal phishing.
nodes: Call the bank immediately to request a recall; file at IC3 for possible fund recovery.

templates.name: Compromised Credentials
templates.description: A user or service account is confirmed in attacker hands.

templates.name: Malware on Endpoint
templates.description: EDR or AV detection of malicious code on a workstation or server.
nodes: Close as false positive; tune the detection

templates.name: Web Application Compromise
templates.description: Exploitation of an internet-facing application, possibly with a web shell.

templates.name: Data Theft Extortion
templates.description: An attacker claims to have stolen data and demands payment, with no encryption.

templates.name: Software Supply Chain Compromise
templates.description: A trusted vendor update or package turns out to be malicious.
